questions.question: What was the significance of Coonan cross oath in Indian church history?
questions.solution_html:
• Coonan Cross Oath (1653)
  • The Coonan cross oath on 3rd January 1653 is the historic revolt of the St.
  • Thomas Christmas against the imposition of Latin rule.
  • This was the culmination of the general unrest felt among the St. Thomas
  • Christians due to the enforced decisions of the Synod of Diamper.
  • The Malabar Christians became enraged and assembled before a cross at
  • Mattancherry near Cochin on January 3rd 1653 and holding a rope tied to the
  • cross swear that they
  • would no more be subordinate to the Latin rule in Church life.
  • This event 1653 broke the 50 years old Roman supremacy imposed at the Synod
  • of Diamper in 1599.

questions.question: Write short notes anyone of the following? a) Synod of Diamper b) Syrian Colonization
questions.solution_html:
• SYNOD OF DIAMPER
  • .1599 June 20, Arch bishop Alexis de Menezes conveyed a council of the
  • church representatives to make them to agree to come under pope.
  • . Synod started at udayamperor, The St Thomas Christians revolted against it.
  • . Through this synod St Thomas Christians accept the Latin liturgy, nine matters
  • affected the ST. Thomas Christians church
  • SYRIAN COLONIZATION’S
  • Immigration of Syrian Christians from Persia under Thomas of Cana:
  • The St. Thomas Christians of Malabar had trade connections with the Syrians of
  • Persia and Babylon. This relation became more intimate because of immigration
  • of Christians from Persia in the 4th Century.
  • The arrival of these colonists increased the prestige and strength of the
  • Malabar church. .It helped the Malabar church to carry on commercial relations
  • and trade with foreign countries like Egypt, Venice etc
  • It paved the way for the emergence of two sets of Christians in India
  • namely the ‘Thekkumbhagakkar’ and ‘Vadakkumbhagakar’.
  • Immigration of the Syrian Christians in the 9th Century. In
  • 825 A. D. a group of Christians from Persia reached Malabar under the leadership
  • of a merchant Sabariso.
